comparison.objective: Moves two backlash-affected sliders to target readings and locks each dial; the candidate sets one gripper stop and secures it mechanically.
comparison.physical_skill: PR-779 requires reversal-aware compensation of display hysteresis and button presses; the candidate requires physical driver/wrench engagement and opposing torque on coupled threads.
comparison.success_condition: PR-779 checks both displayed setpoints within ±2.5 mm and latched lock buttons; the candidate checks a locked 90° opening, ≤2° drift, and three actuation cycles.
comparison.reason: Both contain setpoints and locking, but software-display backlash compensation with pushbutton latching does not test mechanical jam-nut countertorque or functional stop retention.

review_notes: Historical backlash-dial-setpoint: fetch original if relevant; no assumed distinct.
